newsitem.title: USA: CME panel to discuss earlier S&P 500 futures open.
newsitem.headline: CME panel to discuss earlier S&P 500 futures open.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange equity indices committee will hear a presentation on Wednesday weighing the pros and cons of opening Standard and Poor's 500 futures trading 70 minutes earlier, exchange sources said.

S&P 500 futures currently open at 0830 CST/1430 GMT, but a trading hours subcommittee has been investigating the costs and benefits of opening at 0720 CST/1320 GMT, said Jack Bouroudjian, vice president of equity derivatives at Credit Agricole and a CME director. The subcommittee will present its preliminary findings to the equity committee on Wednesday.
The extra trading time would open the futures market before the earliest U.S. economic news releases and at the same time as Treasury bond and Eurodollar futures.
Bouroudjian said the earlier trading hours issue was in its early stages, and called the subcommittee's presentation to the committee merely informative.

The S&P 500 futures pit was abuzz with the issue on Tuesday. Some traders said an earlier open could be an opportunity to capture more business during sessions that include early U.S. economic releases.
U.S. payrolls data and other critical reports are released at 0730 CST.
Bouroudjian said an earlier opening could offer more liquid markets during those sessions, "but it could be a hard sell for us to open before the stock market."
Some traders said that because the S&P 500 futures product at the CME was a derivative of the New York Stock Exchange's stock market, it should not open earlier than that market.
"We don't want to anger the dog," an S&P 500 trader said. "We are the tail and they might not like the idea of an opening earlier than the stock market."
S&P 500 futures trading closes at 1530 CST, 15 minutes after the cash market closes.

Bouroudjian said futures commissions merchants (FCMs) may oppose an earlier opening since GLOBEX trading is currently available in S&Ps after economic releases. Bouroudjian said FCMs may object to earlier pit trading because it costs more to staff a trading floor for an hour than to staff a GLOBEX station.
"It isn't a big deal yet, frankly," he said. "Right now what we are engaging in is a Socratic dialogue," Bouroudjian said.
